newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Bloemenveiling flower market grew six pct in '96.
newsitem.headline: Bloemenveiling flower market grew six pct in '96.

text.p: The Bloemenveiling Holland - the second largest flower market in the Netherlands - has seen a six percent growth in turnover for 1996, the auction said in its annual results report.
And this year the market expects growing demand, especially from eastern Europe and an increased supply of flowers and plants from Africa, Israel, Ecuador and India.
Representing both Naadwijk and Bleiswijk markets, Bloemenveiling Holland is the second largest flower auction in the Netherlands after Aalsmeer.

Last year, the turnover of Bloemenveiling Holland was 2.2 billion Dutch guilders ($1.1 billion) which had increased by 130 million guilders or six percent on 1995's turnover levels. Total operational income was 17 million guilders at the co-operative.
This was largely due to increased volumes and better prices. Weather conditions and a higher sales of garden plants also led to the good results, the market said.
But Bloemenveiling Holland said that all of its energy now has to be put into keeping the auction in a leading position.
"The positive results do not mean the market can relax as a lot of growers see their profits under pressure and a lot of them are searching for new exports, it stated.

In total, the auction handled 3.7 billion cut flowers and 240 million houseplants and 138 million garden plants. The total number of plants and flowers was 4.08 billion pieces compared to 3.98 billion in 1995.
Foreign flower imports increased at the market in 1996 to 635 million pieces from 557 million in 1995.
The market dropped restrictions on imports on July one last year when it changed its policy as it believed that increasing imports cannot be avoided.

The market, where 1,660 people are employed, has a 38 percent share of the market. whereas Bloemenveiling Aalsmeer, the Dutch leader, has a 44 percent share. The Flora market lies in third place with a market share of 11 percent.
All of the major export markets in Europe bought more flowers last year at the Dutch auctions.
The value of flower and plant exports in millions of guilders with percent change from 1995 from all Dutch auctions to top European country markets included:
Million guilders Pct change on '95
Germany 3,200 up 4.8
France 971 up 13.3
Italy 283 up 8.5
Austria 261 up 9.6
